title: Join two aluminium strips with a pop rivet: hold the riveter square, pump it till the stem snaps, bin the stem
instruction: Rivet the two strips together through the drilled hole with a blind rivet from the holder, then put the riveter back.
context: Blind (pop) rivets join sheet metal wherever only one side can be reached: ducts, aircraft skins, trailers, enclosures. Setting one by hand has a standard: the riveter held square and pressed on the rivet's head while its handles are pumped till the stem snaps, or the rivet sets crooked or loose; and the spent stem binned, not left in the tool or on the work as debris. Done by: sheet metal workers (O*NET 47-2211.00), aircraft structures assemblers and mechanics (51-2011.00, 49-3011.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. Work: two aluminium strips (12 x 3 x 0.15 cm each, along y) stacked on a wooden block (8 x 14 x 3.5 cm) and held by two steel clamp jaws at their ends, all fixed, at x 27, y 0; a 4.9 mm hole through both strips at their middle, a bore in the block below it. Rivets: two 4.8 x 8 mm dome-head blind rivets (aluminium body, zinc-plated steel mandrel 2.7 mm across and 28 mm long overall; 9.5 mm head, 8 mm shank; rated grip range 2.0-3.5 mm, for the 3.0 mm of the two strips), stem up in a wooden holder (3 x 4 x 2 cm) at x 21, y -5.8 and -4.2. Hand riveter: a plier-type riveter (0.42 kg: red cast head, zinc nosepiece, a fixed handle and a sprung handle with 3 cm wide black vinyl grips, 14 cm tall), nose down in a wooden holster (6 x 6 x 4 cm with a rim) at x 18, y -14, its handles side by side along x, the sprung one towards the robot. Scrap tray: steel, 6 x 4.5 cm, 1.5 cm deep, at x 32, y -11.
scoring: Measured at the end by looking at the rivet and the strips, the tray and the holster. 0 if at any point the rivet was pulled with the riveter tilted over 6 degrees or not pressed on its head (set crooked or loose: it cannot be fixed but by drilling it out). Otherwise: 1.0 if the rivet is set (its stem snapped) through both strips, the spent stem lies in the scrap tray, and the riveter stands back in its holster with no part of either gripper within 1 cm of it, still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s; 0.5 if the rivet is set but the stem is not in the tray (left in the riveter, on the work or the bench) or the riveter is not back; 0.25 if a rivet is in the hole but not set; else 0.
reset_notes: Drill out the set rivet (or use fresh strips), empty the tray, put two rivets in the holder and stand the riveter in its holster with its handles open.
fidelity: PhysX cannot pull a rivet's stem: our model loads a rivet when the nose is lowered over its stem (within 3 mm, its mouth guiding it), lets the rivet into the hole within 1.5 mm, holds the nose on the rivet, pulls the stem 5.7 mm per radian the handles close and sets it at 6 mm; tilted or lifted pulls spoil it. Forces scaled to the arms. The nose is drawn only; boxes; grips friction 1.0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm moves over the riveter's holster and the strips but never grips anything; the riveter stays in its holster); demo: 1.0 (success at step 810)
